### Refresher cont'd: The Research Process

.font110[The journey from question to insight follows these essential steps:]

.font80[
<div class="chev-flow">
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("circle-question", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>1. Ask a Question</strong><br>
    Formulate a clear, specific question worth investigating.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step chev-step-highlight">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("magnifying-glass", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>2. Gather Information</strong><br>
    Review the literature & collect relevant data through appropriate methods.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("chart-line", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>3. Analyze the Information</strong><br>
    Examine data for patterns, trends, and meaning.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("lightbulb", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>4. Draw Conclusions</strong><br>
    Develop evidence-based answers to your original question.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("share-nodes", height = "1.6em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>5. Share Findings</strong><br>
    Communicate results effectively to appropriate audiences.</p>
  </div>
</div>
]

# Literature Review `r top_icon("book")`

### What is it? &nbsp;•&nbsp; How to do it? &nbsp;•&nbsp; How to do it well?

---
### What is a Literature Review?

.pull-left[
<img src="assets/lit-template-reading.png" width="60%" style="border-radius: 6px;">
]

.pull-right[
.font90[
A **literature review** is a summary and analysis of what has *already* been written on a topic.

It helps you:
- Understand what's already known
- See where there are gaps or debates
- Avoid repeating others' work
- Build a strong foundation for your own research
]
]

---
### How to Conduct a Lit Review

.font90[
**Step 1: Clarify Your Topic or Research Question**

**Step 2: Search for Reliable Sources**

**Step 3: Skim and Select**
- Read abstracts first to decide if the source is relevant.
- Choose a mix of recent, relevant, and diverse perspectives.
- Aim for at least **5–10 solid sources** (depending on assignment length).
]


---
### Reliable vs. Unreliable Sources

.pull-left[
.content-box-blue[
### `r fontawesome::fa("circle-check", height = "1em", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Reliable Sources

- Backed by verifiable evidence
- Created by experts
- Undergo review processes
- Transparent about methods
- Cite their sources
]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-yellow[
### `r fontawesome::fa("triangle-exclamation", height = "1em")` Unreliable Sources

- Lack transparency
- Anonymous or unclear authorship
- Sensationalist language
- One-sided arguments
- Missing citations
]
]

---
### Examples of Reliable Sources

.font70[
<div class="logo-grid">
  <div class="logo-card"><img src="assets/logo-1.png"><p><strong>CDC</strong><br>Centers for Disease Control and Prevention</p></div>
  <div class="logo-card"><img src="assets/logo-2.png"><p><strong>NASA</strong><br>National Aeronautics and Space Administration</p></div>
  <div class="logo-card"><img src="assets/logo-3.png"><p><strong>NEJM</strong><br>Academic Medical Journal</p></div>
  <div class="logo-card"><img src="assets/logo-4.png"><p><strong>US Census Bureau</strong><br>Federal Statistical Agency</p></div>
  <div class="logo-card"><img src="assets/logo-5.png"><p><strong>WHO</strong><br>World Health Organization</p></div>
  <div class="logo-card"><img src="assets/logo-6.png"><p><strong>National Geographic</strong><br>Science and Education Publication</p></div>
  <div class="logo-card"><img src="assets/logo-7.png"><p><strong>Smithsonian</strong><br>Research and Museum Institution</p></div>
  <div class="logo-card"><img src="assets/logo-8.png"><p><strong>APA</strong><br>American Psychological Association</p></div>
</div>
]

.font80[.center[These institutions are known for rigorous research methods, expert review processes, and commitment to accuracy in their published information.]]

---
### Why Source Evaluation Matters

.font90[
<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev-sm">`r fontawesome::fa("trophy", height = "1.4em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Credible Research</strong><br>
  Strong sources lead to respected conclusions.</div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev-sm">`r fontawesome::fa("shield-halved", height = "1.4em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Protection from Misinformation</strong><br>
  Critical evaluation prevents spreading falsehoods.</div>
</div>

<div class="chev-row">
  <div class="chev-sm">`r fontawesome::fa("brain", height = "1.4em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
  <div class="chev-text"><strong>Critical Thinking Development</strong><br>
  Evaluating sources builds essential life skills.</div>
</div>
]

---
### Red Flags of Misinformation

.pull-left[
<img src="assets/lit-redflags-caution.png" width="60%" style="border-radius: 6px;">
]

.pull-right[
.font90[
**`r fontawesome::fa("triangle-exclamation", fill = "#D55E00")` Sensational Language**<br>
.font80["You won't believe this!" or excessive punctuation for shock value.]

**`r fontawesome::fa("circle-question", fill = "#0148A4")` Missing Attribution**<br>
.font80[No clear author, source, or supporting evidence.]

**`r fontawesome::fa("arrows-left-right", fill = "#0148A4")` One-Sided Presentation**<br>
.font80[No acknowledgment of alternative perspectives or debates.]

**`r fontawesome::fa("bolt", fill = "#D55E00")` Extraordinary Claims**<br>
.font80[Bold statements without proportional evidence.]
]
]

---
### Types of Sources

.pull-left[
.content-box-blue[
#### `r fontawesome::fa("layer-group", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Primary / Secondary / Tertiary

- **Primary:** original work or raw data (e.g., a study, a diary, survey results)
- **Secondary:** interprets or analyzes primary work (e.g., a review article)
- **Tertiary:** compiles & summarizes (e.g., encyclopedias, textbooks)
]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-green[
#### `r fontawesome::fa("scale-balanced", fill = "#2C5F2D")` Peer-Reviewed vs. Grey Literature

- **Peer-reviewed:** vetted by experts before publication
- **Grey literature:** reports, working papers, government & NGO documents — useful, but evaluate carefully
]
]

---
### Anatomy of an Academic Article

.font90[One of today's goals: understand the **basic structure** of an academic article.]

.font85[
<div class="chev-flow">
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("align-left", height = "1.4em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>Abstract</strong><br>The whole study in a paragraph.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("circle-question", height = "1.4em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>Intro</strong><br>The question & why it matters.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("flask", height = "1.4em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>Methods</strong><br>How they studied it.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("chart-column", height = "1.4em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>Results</strong><br>What they found.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="chev-step">
    <div class="chev-right">`r fontawesome::fa("lightbulb", height = "1.4em", fill = "#0148A4")`</div>
    <p><strong>Discussion</strong><br>What it means.</p>
  </div>
</div>
]

---
### How to Read an Abstract Efficiently

.pull-left[
.font90[
Skim the abstract and ask four questions:

1. **What was the research question?**
2. **How did they study it?**
3. **What did they find?**
4. **What did they conclude?**
]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-yellow[
#### `r fontawesome::fa("stopwatch", fill = "#0148A4")` Activity: Speed-Read!

Read an abstract in **90 seconds** and answer the four questions above.
]
]

---
### How to Conduct a Lit Review

.center[
  .orange[From the start]
  ]
.font90[
**Step 1: Clarify Your Topic or Research Question**

**Step 2: Search for Reliable Sources**

**Step 3: Skim and Select**
- Read abstracts first to decide if the source is relevant.
- Choose a mix of recent, relevant, and diverse perspectives.
- Aim for at least **5–10 solid sources** (depending on assignment length).
]

---
### How to Conduct a Lit Review

.font85[
**Step 4: Take Notes**
- Write down the main point of each source.
- Note how it relates to your topic, and any key quotes or data.
- Use color coding or a chart to organize themes or arguments.

**Step 5: Group by Themes or Ideas**
- Don't stop at summarizing each article one by one.
- Instead, group your notes by common themes, disagreements, or trends.
- Ask: *What do these sources have in common? How do they differ?*

**Step 6: Start Writing**

**Step 7: Cite Everything** .font80[(we will cover *how* next week)]
]

---
### Literature Review Template .font60[(Short Version)]

.pull-left[
<img src="assets/lit-compass-research.png" width="60%" style="border-radius: 6px;">
]

.pull-right[
.font90[
**Begin with a short introduction**
- What is your topic?
- Why is it important?

**Body**
- Share what other studies have found.
- Organize by **themes, not by author**.

**Summary**
- Clarify how *your* project connects to past research.
]
]

---

</div>
]

.content-box-blue[Use **Wikipedia** as an *entry point* only — then follow its references to reliable sources. Track everything with the **Source Tracker** handout.]
]

---
### Efficient Literature Search

.pull-left[
<img src="assets/lit-efficient-search.png" width="60%" style="border-radius: 6px;">
]

.pull-right[
.font80[
**`r fontawesome::fa("key", fill = "#0148A4")` Smart Keywords**
- Pick keywords that find the right content
- Try synonyms
- Use quotation marks: *"Climate Change"*

**`r fontawesome::fa("bullseye", fill = "#0148A4")` Intentional Sources**
- Google Scholar (if available)
- Library databases (and use filters)
- Trusted `.edu` / `.gov` / organization sites

**`r fontawesome::fa("book-open", fill = "#0148A4")` Initial Reading**
- Abstract, conclusions, and graphs first
- Track & "rate" finds in your **Source Tracker** ;)
]
]

class: middle

### `r fontawesome::fa("magnifying-glass-location", fill = "#0148A4")` Activity: Scavenger Hunting!

.content-box-yellow[
.font90[
Let's see how your **key variables** are defined by the experts — and find an article that examines your research question (or a related one).

**Use your Source Tracker doc!**

**Must find:**
1. One **peer-reviewed** source
2. One **government / institutional** data source
]
]

---
### `r fontawesome::fa("people-group", fill = "#0148A4")` After-Class Team Session .font60[(3:15 – 5:15 PM)]

.pull-left[
<img src="assets/lit-homework-team.png" width="60%" style="border-radius: 6px;">
]

.pull-right[
.font85[
Work with your **TA / peer mentor** — produce a **tangible output** before dinner (*not* free time).

- Begin the **Team Literature Review Template** — each member contributes **1 source summary** (author, year, finding, relevance to your question).
- Search **Google Scholar** or **PubMed** for **2 additional sources**.
- Apply the **CRAAP test** to assess quality *before* logging each source.
]
]

---
### `r fontawesome::fa("moon", fill = "#0148A4")` Evening Work Period .font60[(7:00 – 9:00 PM)]

.font90[Individual + partner work during **CTD RTA study hours**. TA available for drop-in questions.]

.pull-left[
.content-box-blue[
.font85[
#### `r fontawesome::fa("clipboard-list", fill = "#4a7fb5")` Individual Mission Sheet

**Part 1 — Search Strategy**<br>
Document keywords used, databases searched, and quality criteria applied.

**Part 2 — Key Source**<br>
Identify one important article, assess its quality, and summarize **one finding in your own words**.
]
]
]

.pull-right[
.content-box-yellow[
.font85[
#### `r fontawesome::fa("pen-nib", fill = "#0148A4")` Research Cycle Sheet (RcS)

Write the **"Beginning"** paragraph of your literature review:

- Introduce your topic
- Define your variables
- Include **2+ citations** in **APA format**
]
]
]

### `r fontawesome::fa("comments", fill = "#0148A4")` Activity: Scientific Storytelling

.content-box-blue[
.font90[
Each team member writes a **2-sentence summary** of one source they found:

1. What was the study about?
2. What did it find?

**Sentence starter:** *"According to [Author, Year], researchers found that..."*

Then **read it aloud** to a partner. Practice a tone that is **formal but accessible**.
]
